Almond Cookies

Served at: St. Lucia's Day

Makes about 24 cookiesPrep 15 minCook 12 min

Almond Cookies are a beloved treat traditionally served during St. Lucia's Day celebrations in Sweden and other Scandinavian countries. These crisp, buttery cookies flavored with almond extract honor the festive spirit of the holiday, which celebrates light and hope in the dark winter months.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, softened
  • 3/4 cup granulated sugar
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 teaspoon almond extract
  • 2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup sliced almonds

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. In a large bowl, cream together the softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
  3. Beat in the egg and almond extract until well combined.
  4. In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
  5. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture, stirring until a soft dough forms.
  6. Roll the dough into 1-inch (2.5 cm) balls and place them 2 inches (5 cm) apart on the prepared baking sheet.
  7. Flatten each ball slightly with the palm of your hand or the bottom of a glass.
  8. Press a few sliced almonds onto the top of each cookie.
  9. Bake for 10-12 minutes or until the edges are lightly golden.
  10. Allow the cookies to cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

Tips

  • For extra almond flavor, sprinkle a tiny bit of almond extract on top before baking.
  • Store cookies in an airtight container to keep them crisp for up to a week.
  • You can substitute sliced almonds with chopped whole almonds if preferred.
